name: Why does my kitchen feel crowded even though it has plenty of cabinets?

mainEntity.name: Why does my kitchen feel crowded even though it has plenty of cabinets?

acceptedAnswer.text: A kitchen can feel crowded because of poor circulation, oversized appliances, deep cabinets, door swings, or too many competing routes—not only because the room is small. Start by identifying where people pass, where doors collide, and where preparation stops during cooking. Reducing a cabinet depth, changing a door swing, resizing an appliance, or removing an unnecessary peninsula may help more than adding square footage. Test changes with tape and full-size appliance templates. Elite Remodeling & Design can evaluate circulation as part of a complete layout redesign.
acceptedAnswer.description: Crowding often comes from circulation conflicts, deep cabinets, oversized appliances, door swings, or poorly placed islands. Map traffic and open doors, then test smaller-depth storage, revised swings, appliance changes, or a shorter peninsula before expanding the room.
